stemMd: Why does the small intestine have villi and microvilli?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They prevent any blood from reaching the intestine.

options.label: C
options.textMd: They store chromosomes for liver cells.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They make the intestinal contents completely dry.

options.label: E
options.textMd: They increase the surface area available for absorption.

explanationMd: Villi are tissue projections and microvilli are smaller projections on epithelial cells. Both expand the interface across which digested nutrients can be absorbed. The folds improve capacity without requiring a correspondingly large increase in the organ’s external dimensions.

distractorRationale.a: Absorbed nutrients must be transported away by blood or lymph.
distractorRationale.b: Surface area does not replace chemical digestion.
distractorRationale.c: Intestinal projections do not store another organ’s chromosomes.
distractorRationale.d: Their primary role is enhanced absorption, not complete drying.
